page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. One marginal note in the left margin, beside the paragraph beginning "Johan." Running head at top right, page number at top left.

main_text.p: morte Christi differit, & ait, Christum factum esse hominem, ut mortem perpeti posset, et subdit, Deum ex gratuita Misericordia Christum nobis ordinasse in Sacerdotem, qui sacrificio sua mortis expiaret omnium nostrum peccata, gustando pro illis mortem, ac iram Dei adversus peccata nostra, qua ipse ut Sponsor in se receperat.

His ita stantibus, nō eo inficias, nos benignitate Dei maximum beneficium consecutos esse ex morte Christi, cum propter ipsam mortem Christus gloria & honore coronatus fuerit, ideo nos quoq; gloria & honore coronabi-mur suo tempore: Sed simul intelligo, eum ꝓ[?] peccatis nostris expiandis gu-stasse mortem.

§. Testim.Johan. 10. 15. Ego animam meam, id est, vitam depono pro ovibus. Et Johan. 17. 19. Pro eis ego sanctifico me ipsum, ut sint & ipsi sanctificati per veritatem. Pro eis, scilicet, ut eis promerear apud te remissionem peccatorum, & vitam æternam. Uti Christus ipse, in institutione sacræ cœnæ, exponit præpositionem ἀντί, positam ꝓ ὑπὲρ[?], cum ait: Hoc est sanguis meus novi Testamenti, qui pro multis effunditur in re-missi-

page.notes: Printed ꝓ before "peccatis" (ꝓ[?]) read as pro; the mark could also be per. Greek words "ἀντί" and "ὑπὲρ" are read from a small, faint print; accents and breathings uncertain. The sign after "exponit praepositionem" and the Greek after "positam" are the least certain readings on the page. The marginal note "§. Testim." is printed in heavy italic. Printed hyphen in "gu-stasse" appears as a slash-like mark at the line end.
